transcript.text: Indesit washer dryer washes fine but the drying cycle doesn't get warm at all, clothes come out cold and wet after 2 hours. Model is XWDE 96 something.

1. 2. The cut-out usually trips because fluff has built up and restricted the airflow, so it's often the symptom rather than the root cause.
3. Something simpler is going on: too big a load, clothes not spun properly, or a short or low-heat dry setting. One thing worth knowing is that most washer-dryers finish drying with a cool-down phase. So clothes that come out cool at the end don't prove there was no heat. Feeling the machine while it's actually drying tells you far more. 1. Feel for heat mid-cycle. Start a full drying programme and, after 20–30 minutes, carefully touch the door glass and the top of the machine (it can get hot). The problem is airflow, load or condensing, which is often easy to fix. • Stone cold: it points to the heater, thermostat or cut-out. 2. Check the clothes before drying starts. Run a wash only and look at the clothes after the final spin. They should be damp, not dripping. If they're soaking, the real fault is on the spin or drain side, not drying. 3. Check the load and the programme. A washer-dryer dries much less than it washes, typically about half to two-thirds of the wash load. The dry capacity is usually printed on the front or in the manual. Try a small load, around half the drum, on a full cotton/'cupboard dry' setting rather than a short timed or delicates dry. 4. Clean the pump filter (bottom front). Drying fluff often ends up there and can restrict the drying airflow. • Switch off and unplug the machine first. • Lay towels down and have a shallow tray ready. • Unscrew the filter slowly and clear any fluff. Also make sure the cold tap is on and the hose isn't kinked, as the condensing side needs that water. If the clothes spin properly, the load is modest, the filter is clean and the machine still stays completely cold while drying, that's a fairly clear heater-side fault (element, thermostat or cut-out). Those parts sit inside the machine behind the casing, so at that point most people are better off with an engineer unless you're confident with appliance repairs. claimsRejected.claim: The drying heater element has failed.
Its thermostat has failed, or a thermal cut-out has tripped.

candidates: Drying heater element failed (no heat at all) (medium)
Drying thermostat or tripped thermal cut-out, often after fluff restricting the airflow (medium)
Load, spin or programme problem (dry load too big, clothes not spun, short or low-heat dry setting) (low)

reading.symptom: drying cycle doesn't heat, clothes cold and wet

plan: Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Indesit; model XWDE 96.
The fault they reported is: "drying cycle doesn't heat, clothes cold and wet". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
